title: Why a sale makes you spend more

scenes.say: Half off didn't save you money.
You weren't shopping for a jacket. Then you saw it. Two hundred dollars, crossed out. One hundred today.
That first number is an anchor. Your brain uses it as the reference point, even though the store picked it.
Economist Richard Thaler called the next part transaction utility. Enjoying the deal itself, not the thing you bought.

data.title: Transaction utility
data.footer: You enjoy the deal, not the jacket.

scenes.say: Add, ends tonight, and imagined regret pushes you to act.
Anchor. Deal pleasure. Regret. None of them is about the jacket.

data.footer: None of them is about the jacket.

scenes.say: So ask: would I want it at one hundred, if it had never cost two hundred?

data.text: Would you want it at $100 if it had never cost $200?
